title: Route-level A/B testing (Route Experiments) — GA requirements + cross-team acceptance criteria
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Goal
Ship Route-level A/B testing ("Route Experiments") to GA with the minimum required safety, permissions, auditability, telemetry correctness, and customer-facing docs/support readiness.

This ticket is the GA gate checklist. Engineering tickets implement features; this ticket defines the product acceptance criteria and cross-team deliverables required to flip GA defaults (region-by-region rollout) and announce externally.

References
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/route-level-ab-testing-prd.json
- UX spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-route-experiments-ux-spec.json
- ADR-047 deterministic bucketing: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-047-deterministic-experiment-bucketing.json
- ADR-048 metrics attribution schema: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-048-experiment-metrics-attribution-schema.json
- Experiment service overview: sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/experiment-service-overview.json
- Audit requirements: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/experiment-config-audit-events.json
- Dashboards/alerts spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/experiment-health-dashboards-spec.json
- GA launch checklist (release eng): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/console-rollouts-ga-launch-checklist-route-experiments.json

Non-goals (explicit GA cut line)
- No full statistical significance engine in Console (beyond basic deltas + guardrail thresholds).
- No customer-defined custom metric ingestion (Redwood-defined metrics + Redwood eval signals only).
- No multi-region cross-population rebalancing (deterministic bucketing only).

GA entry criteria (must-have)
1) Core experiment lifecycle in Console is complete
- Create experiment (route selector + variants + allocation + eligibility/stickiness) behind GA-default feature flag state.
- Start/stop semantics are clear and safe; intermediate states displayed (Starting/Running/Stopping/Stopped).
- Stop behavior: "immediate stop" is allowed; draining semantics are not required for GA but must be documented if implemented.
- Overlapping experiments on the same route: behavior is deterministic and enforced by validation (either blocked or priority-based). GA requirement: Console must prevent accidental overlap by default (block) unless an explicit override is implemented with strong warning copy.

Acceptance criteria
- From a clean account (no beta flags), an Org Admin can create and run an experiment end-to-end without support intervention.
- Validation error messages are actionable (tell the user what field is wrong + how to fix).
- Console provides an obvious "Stop experiment" affordance with confirmation and clear blast radius messaging (routes impacted, expected rollback behavior).

2) Deterministic assignment + routing precedence is stable
- Stickiness key precedence matches ADR-047 and is documented (e.g., explicit sticky key/header > customer_id/org user key > session key > safe fallback).
- If stickiness key is missing/low entropy, system behavior must not cause severe skew; Console surfaces warnings and/or enforces minimum entropy requirements.
- Precedence with canary rollouts/fallback policies is consistent: experiment variant selection occurs before fallback evaluation (per routing PR), and the final resolution is explainable.

Acceptance criteria
- Repeated requests with the same stickiness key consistently map to the same variant across restarts.
- Split accuracy within tolerance under synthetic load tests (define target tolerance: +/- 2% absolute for each variant at 50k+ requests).
- Cross-region determinism: same key produces same variant across regions given the same experiment config version.

3) Telemetry correctness + attribution schema is GA-ready
- Canonical attribution dimensions emitted consistently for request + streaming + retries:
  - route_id (normalized template)
  - experiment_id
  - variant_id
  - model_id
  - region
- Attribution drop rate is measured and alertable.
- Metrics cardinality controls are in place (limit tag explosion; sampling strategy where needed).

Acceptance criteria
- Attribution drop rate for eligible traffic is <= 0.5% over a 24h window in at least two production regions during ramp.
- For streaming requests + retries, experiment_id/variant_id persist through retry paths.
- Query cost for results view does not cause DB load spikes (guardrails: p95 results API < 2s; no sustained DB CPU > agreed threshold during internal load).

4) Guardrails + auto-stop behavior is safe and aligns with product promise
- GA default guardrail behavior: soft-stop + notification (no automatic hard-stop by default).
- Optional hard-stop for severe regressions may exist but must be behind:
  - kill switch
  - explicit enablement per account/org
  - documented semantics and false-positive guidance
- Guardrails supported in Console:
  - latency (p95/p99)
  - error rate
  - cost/token (as defined by telemetry/cost attribution)
  - optional quality signal if eval integration enabled

Acceptance criteria
- Guardrail configuration is visible at a glance in experiment details.
- When a guardrail triggers:
  - experiment status becomes "Degraded" (or equivalent)
  - Console shows which guardrail fired, threshold, current value, evaluation window
  - alert/runbook link is present
- Guardrail evaluation windows and alert noise are tuned to avoid flapping during low traffic.

5) RBAC + permissions are enforced end-to-end
- Permissions must cover: create, update, start, stop, delete, view results, view audit trail, access debug endpoint (internal only).
- GA requirement: least privilege aligned with enterprise roles; "break-glass" admin path documented.

Acceptance criteria
- A user without mutation permissions cannot create/start/stop via Console or API (server-side enforced).
- Read-only roles can view experiments and results but cannot see sensitive debug details.
- Permission denied states are user-friendly in Console (correct empty states + call-to-action to request access).

6) Audit logging meets enterprise compliance baseline
- Audit events for: create/update/start/stop/delete.
- Required fields (per security doc): actor, actor_type, org_id, timestamp, experiment identifiers, affected routes, before/after diff summary (redacted where appropriate), request_id/trace_id link.
- Retention/export format supported for enterprise (SIEM-friendly; confirm field names are stable).

Acceptance criteria
- Every mutation produces an audit event accessible in Console audit view and export pipeline.
- Audit export includes experiment_id/variant_id and change summary; sensitive payload fields are redacted.
- Internal debug endpoint exposure is gated and audited.

7) Observability: standard dashboards + alerts + runbooks are live
- Grafana dashboards include:
  - per-variant latency/cost/error
  - attribution drop rate
  - propagation lag/staleness
  - variant 0 traffic detection / zero-traffic variant detection
- Alerts include:
  - propagation lag above threshold
  - attribution anomalies (drop rate, sudden cardinality spike)
  - severe p99 latency regression when hard-stop enabled
- Runbooks are complete and linked from alert payloads and Console guardrail banners.

Acceptance criteria
- On-call can diagnose: skewed allocation, sticky-key drift, config propagation issues, missing attribution, expensive queries.
- All alerts have an owner, severity, and escalation policy.

8) Documentation + DX are GA-ready
- Customer guide shipped (incl. SDK notes on stickiness keys and interpreting variant headers).
- Troubleshooting section covers top beta issues:
  - missing headers / missing attribution
  - streaming retry attribution
  - skew when stickiness key missing
  - propagation lag / stale results
- Example app exists or is linked.

Acceptance criteria
- Docs reviewed by DevEx + Support; includes copy for variant headers and "how to confirm assignment".
- Support macros / internal FAQ updated with known issues and resolution steps.

9) Results view correctness + basic deltas
- Results API returns per-variant metrics + deltas vs control over selected time window.
- Console results view supports drill-down by route/model/region (at least route + variant + region for GA).
- Data freshness expectations are communicated (aggregation window + expected delay).

Acceptance criteria
- Console clearly indicates last updated timestamp and aggregation window.
- "Results not updating" state provides actionable guidance (e.g., check propagation lag; link to runbook).

Cross-team deliverables (who/what)
- Console & Tooling (Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin / Felix Schneider): GA UX polish, results view performance, audit view.
- Platform / Policy Engine (Ethan Park / Jordan Lee / Mina Haddad): deterministic assignment, precedence rules, config propagation behavior.
- Telemetry & Analytics (Logan Wright / Caleb Johnson / Mei Lin / Nadia Rahman): attribution correctness, rollups, cardinality controls, backfill plan if needed.
- SRE/Observability (Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes / Allison Grant / Aisha Bello): SLOs, dashboards, alerts, runbooks, game day sign-off.
- Security (Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei): audit events, export fields, redaction, debug endpoint gating.
- Applied ML/Evals (Dr. Maya Srinivasan / Jonas Weber / Selene Huang): optional quality signal wiring + quality regression alert definition (GA optional but must not break core flows).
- Release coordination (Connor O'Brien): feature flag plan, staged enablement, rollout by region/account tier, rollback criteria.

GA sign-off checklist (final gate)
- [ ] Feature flag default is ON for eligible tiers/regions per rollout plan; allowlist removed.
- [ ] SLOs met for control plane APIs and config propagation staleness bounds.
- [ ] Attribution drop rate <= target and stable for 7 days during ramp.
- [ ] Audit logs validated in export pipeline with security sign-off.
- [ ] RBAC validated with at least 3 roles (Admin, Operator, Read-only) via real org accounts.
- [ ] Dashboards and alerts are live in prod with runbook links.
- [ ] Docs published + support readiness checklist completed.

Open questions (to resolve before GA)
1) Overlapping experiments policy: hard block vs allow with priority. GA preference: hard block; if allow, must show priority stack and require explicit acknowledgement.
2) Default guardrail thresholds: confirm final recommended defaults (latency/error/cost) and which are required vs optional.
3) Results freshness messaging: confirm expected aggregation delay and user-facing copy.
4) Variant headers: final naming and whether to show in Console/SDK response objects.

Notes from beta learnings to incorporate
- Staging observed propagation lag and attribution drop issues; ensure we have prod monitors and runbooks (see dashboard spec).
- Customer confusion about variant headers; docs + Console tooltip must be crisp.
- Metrics tag cardinality risks: ensure restrictions/sampling are in place prior to widening rollout.

Next steps
- Paula Mendes: align GA gate owners on timeline; create a short weekly GA gate status update.
- Connor O'Brien: confirm region-by-region rollout plan and rollback criteria.
- Sean Gallagher: schedule game day for propagation lag + attribution anomaly scenarios and confirm alert noise is acceptable.
